findings.title: Skill references executable scripts
findings.description: Skill `bootstrap` references scripts or a bundled scripts directory. This establishes an execution *capability*; host inheritance and approval enforcement remain unverified.
findings.attacker_control: Malicious or compromised skill instructions / scripts
findings.impact: Potential local command execution under the host agent identity
findings.recommended_action: Treat as an authority surface: verify whether scripts inherit sensitive environment variables and whether execution requires independent approval.
findings.verify_in_60s: ls the skill directory; confirm whether scripts/ is present and executed.

findings.title: Skill references external URLs
findings.description: Skill `bootstrap` references external URLs. A URL is an exposure indicator, not proof of malicious content.
findings.attacker_control: Compromised remote resource referenced by the skill
findings.impact: Potential instruction injection or data exfiltration guidance
findings.recommended_action: Pin or vendor remote references; treat remote content as untrusted.

findings.title: Instruction text directs hide, bypass, or fetch-execute behavior
findings.description: `bootstrap` contains instruction patterns that hide actions, bypass confirmation, or fetch-and-execute remote content. Review before trusting.
findings.attacker_control: Instruction content in the component itself
findings.impact: Agent may follow injected instructions leading to privileged actions
findings.recommended_action: Rewrite instructions; forbid hide/bypass/remote-exec directives in skills.
findings.verify_in_60s: Search the SKILL.md for hide/bypass/fetch-and-execute phrasing.

findings.title: Download-and-execute pattern in agent surface
findings.description: `bootstrap` references piping a remote download into a shell. That is remote code execution under the agent/host identity if followed.
findings.attacker_control: Remote URL content at fetch time
findings.recommended_action: Vendor and pin scripts; never curl|sh from skills or hooks.
findings.fix_snippet: Replace with a pinned local script checked into the repo.

findings.title: Permission-bypass or auto-approve flag in agent surface
findings.description: `bootstrap` references a flag that disables human approval (e.g. `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--yolo`, auto-approve). That expands effective authority without a corresponding control.
findings.attacker_control: Anyone who can influence the command/config that sets the flag
findings.trust_boundary: Human approval gate → bypassed automated agent
findings.impact: Privileged tool use without interactive confirmation
findings.recommended_action: Remove bypass flags; keep approval required for privileged actions.
findings.verify_in_60s: grep for dangerously-skip-permissions / yolo / autoApprove / bypass.
findings.fix_snippet: Delete the bypass flag; keep interactive or policy-gated approvals.

findings.title: MCP local command sets non-secret environment
findings.description: MCP server `unpinned-demo` is registered with a local command transport. Presence of a local process is a capability observation, not proof of abuse.
findings.attacker_control: Compromised MCP server binary/package or tool-poisoned metadata
findings.impact: Tool calls execute under the MCP process identity with host-granted access
missing_controls: Exact artifact digest of the launched binary/package
Host-side authorization binding for tool arguments
findings.recommended_action: Record as an execution capability; verify host isolation before treating as risk.
findings.verify_in_60s: Open the MCP config and inspect command=`npx` plus env/args.
findings.fix_snippet: Pin the MCP binary/package; drop broad path args; avoid inheriting secrets.

findings.title: MCP server launched via unpinned package installer
findings.description: MCP server `unpinned-demo` uses an unpinned launcher (`npx` -y demo-evil-mcp). A later package publish can change behavior without a config edit (rug-pull risk).
findings.attacker_control: Malicious or compromised package published to the unpinned name
findings.trust_boundary: Host agent → package registry → MCP process
findings.impact: Arbitrary code execution under the host agent identity after a registry update
findings.recommended_action: Pin an exact version or digest; avoid `npx -y` / floating `uvx` tags.
findings.verify_in_60s: grep the MCP JSON for npx -y / uvx and confirm no @version pin.
findings.fix_snippet: Use "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "pkg@1.2.3"] or a local pinned binary.

findings.title: Literal secret-like value in MCP env
findings.description: MCP server `unpinned-demo` appears to embed a literal credential in `env` rather than a placeholder reference. Committed secrets are an immediate exposure.
findings.attacker_control: Anyone with repo or backup access can read the credential
findings.impact: Credential theft and downstream account takeover
findings.recommended_action: Replace literal values with `${ENV}` references; rotate the secret.
findings.verify_in_60s: Open the MCP JSON env block; confirm values are placeholders, not literals.
findings.fix_snippet: Use "API_KEY": "${API_KEY}" and inject from the host secret store.

findings.title: Unpinned MCP launcher with secret-bearing env
findings.description: MCP server `unpinned-demo` combines an unpinned package launcher with secret-like environment values. A registry rug-pull can inherit those secrets without a config change.
findings.attacker_control: Compromised registry package + embedded or inherited credentials
findings.trust_boundary: Package registry → MCP process env → secret material
findings.impact: Credential theft or privileged tool abuse after an unpinned update
findings.recommended_action: Pin the package and replace env literals with ${ENV} references.
findings.verify_in_60s: Confirm npx -y/uvx without pin AND secret-named env keys in the same server.

findings.title: MCP server uses remote endpoint
findings.description: MCP server `cleartext-remote` is configured with a remote URL. This is an external exposure surface; TLS identity and credential forwarding are not verified by this rule.
findings.attacker_control: Compromised remote MCP endpoint or MITM without transport identity
findings.impact: Potential exfiltration or tool abuse via remote MCP
findings.recommended_action: Verify endpoint identity, TLS, OAuth scopes, and whether secrets are forwarded.

findings.title: Remote MCP endpoint uses cleartext HTTP
findings.description: MCP server `cleartext-remote` points at `http://mcp.example.invalid/sse` over HTTP. Tool traffic and any forwarded credentials lack transport confidentiality/integrity.
findings.attacker_control: Network MITM on the path to the MCP endpoint
findings.trust_boundary: Host agent → cleartext network → remote MCP
findings.impact: Credential and tool-argument interception or modification
findings.recommended_action: Use https:// only; reject plain HTTP remote MCP registrations.
findings.verify_in_60s: Confirm the url field starts with https://.

findings.title: Unattended automation or CI workflow present
findings.description: `agent` is unattended CI that also references agent/MCP-related steps. Review triggers, tokens, and whether agent authority can run unattended.
findings.attacker_control: Malicious trigger payload or compromised workflow definition
findings.impact: Actions may run without interactive human approval
findings.recommended_action: Confirm agent/MCP steps need this workflow; pin launchers; least-privilege tokens.

findings.title: pull_request_target workflow invokes agent-related steps
findings.description: CI workflow `agent` uses `pull_request_target` together with observed agent/MCP steps (`uses:` or launcher CLI). Fork PRs can often influence checkout/content while retaining privileged secrets — a classic CI + agent abuse path.
findings.attacker_control: Malicious pull request from a fork
findings.trust_boundary: Fork PR content → privileged workflow + agent tools
findings.impact: Secret theft or privileged agent actions from untrusted PR content
findings.recommended_action: Prefer pull_request; never feed fork PR code to privileged agents.
findings.verify_in_60s: Confirm `on: pull_request_target` and whether agent steps touch PR code.
findings.fix_snippet: Switch to pull_request, or isolate secrets from any PR-controlled checkout.

coverage.layer_honesty: Passive scans establish DECLARED/CONFIGURED authority only. EFFECTIVE and VERIFIED require host or authorized runtime evidence.

limitations: Deterministic rules produce OBSERVED/POTENTIAL findings, not confirmed exploits.
CAPABILITY observations are not vulnerabilities; SECURITY_FINDING requires exposure conditions and missing controls.
Passive scans establish DECLARED/CONFIGURED authority only.
Host EFFECTIVE permissions and VERIFIED runtime behavior remain NOT VERIFIED.
Incomplete adapter coverage means absence of findings is not evidence of safety.
